intro: Initialization scale influences signal growth before any training. Predict that growth without drawing random weights.
task: Compare Xavier and He weight variances and resulting pre-activation variances.
requirements: fan_in and fan_out are integers 1..64; input_variance is nonnegative. Assume independent zero-mean inputs and weights.

Return a 2-by-2 array: rows Xavier, He; columns weight variance, pre-activation variance. Weight variances are 2/(fan_in+fan_out) and 2/fan_in. Pre-activation variance is fan_in*weight_variance*input_variance.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Equal widths
examples.output:
[[0.25, 1.0], [0.5, 2.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Expanding layer
examples.output:
[[0.25, 0.5], [1.0, 2.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Larger input variance
examples.output:
[[0.5, 3.0], [1.0, 6.0]]
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Independent zero-mean contributions have additive variances.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Report variance before ReLU, without another factor of one half.

explanation: Fan-based initialization adjusts scale to the number of connections. The calculation explains why identical weight variance behaves differently in narrow and wide layers.
The assumptions are approximations. Correlation and nonzero means in actual activations can change the observed variance, so use the prediction as a baseline rather than a guarantee.
